roadtool.shape.straight.tooltip: Each click ends a straight piece of road, whatever way the road before it runs.
roadtool.shape.curved.tooltip: Click a control point, then the end: the road leaves towards the control point and arrives coming from it. Ending on a road it meets it in its direction, with an S curve where needed.
roadtool.shape.free.tooltip: Each click bends the road on from the way it runs, without a kink.
roadtool.snap.roads.tooltip: Roads start and end on free spline ends and on free connection points of junctions near the pointer.
roadtool.snap.angles.tooltip: Directions snap to right angles: to the road a new road continues or to a road near its start, else to north. Free roads snap to end straight on or square to their start.
roadtool.snap.guides.tooltip: Free spline ends and connection points of junctions nearby cast guide lines: the road's extension and the line square to it. The pointer snaps onto them and onto where two cross, also where they cross a right-angle direction.
roadtool.corner.tooltip: Straight: where a road turns off the road it continues, the corner is rounded with this radius; that road is cut back for it. 0 leaves a sharp corner. Only roads built in this project are cut back.
roadtool.parallel.off.tooltip: Build only the road you draw.
roadtool.parallel.left.tooltip: Build a second road at the distance below, left of the road you draw.
roadtool.parallel.right.tooltip: Build a second road at the distance below, right of the road you draw.
roadtool.parallel.both.tooltip: Build a road on each side at the distance below.
roadtool.distance.tooltip: How far the parallel roads lie from the road you draw, centre line to centre line, in the same profile
roadtool.opposite.tooltip: The parallel roads run the other way, as the other carriageway of a dual road with one-way profiles
roadtool.height.terrain.tooltip: Every piece of the road starts and ends on the terrain; the terrain itself is not changed.
roadtool.height.smooth.tooltip: Follows the terrain averaged over 100 m, with the gradient changing steadily and no kinks, also where the road continues another. With Fit terrain the ground is cut or banked up to the road.
roadtool.height.manual.tooltip: The height runs evenly from the start to the end height below, whatever the terrain does. Switch off Fit terrain for bridges and overpasses, so the ground stays as it is.
roadtool.end_height.tooltip: Height at the end of each new piece of road in manual mode
roadtool.piece.tooltip: Longer roads are split into splines of at most this length, so they can follow the terrain
roadtool.warn.tooltip: Gradients steeper than this are marked; a check, not a rule
roadtool.fit.tooltip: Lays the ground under the road and a shoulder of about 7 m beside it just below kerb height, as OMSI cuts it away under the road, and cuts or banks up slopes of 1:1.5 beyond. The original terrain stays in the original map; deleting the road brings it back.
roadtool.junctions.tooltip: A road ending on another road joins it with a new T junction; a road crossing another gets crossroads there; a road joining one of another width gets a transition. They are made in the profiles of both roads and stored under Sceneryobjects\Mapforge in your OMSI installation.
roadtool.standalone.tooltip: A road in a chrono variant stands alone: this applies to the base map only
roadtool.hint: Click the points of a road; Esc ends it
roadtool.new_type.tooltip: Opens the road builder: put lanes together into a road type of your own (ADR 049)
roadtool.tab.in_map.tooltip: Profiles this map uses, most used first
roadtool.tab.favorites.tooltip: Profiles you marked with the star
roadtool.tab.mine.tooltip: Road types you made with the road builder, kept under Splines\Mapforge
roadtool.category.oneway.tooltip: Roads whose lanes all run one way, also one carriageway of a dual road
roadtool.category.twolanes.tooltip: Roads with one or two lanes, both ways
roadtool.category.fourlanes.tooltip: Roads with three or four lanes
roadtool.category.sixlanes.tooltip: Roads with five or more lanes
roadtool.category.median.tooltip: Roads with a median between their carriageways
roadtool.category.other.tooltip: Wires, fences, walls and helpers only the OMSI editor shows
roadtool.badge.tooltip: {count, plural, one {# spline of this map uses it} other {# splines of this map use it}}
roadtool.edit.tooltip: Opens the road type in the road builder to change it, with every spline of it
roadtool.empty.sorting: Sorting the profiles of the installation...
roadtool.empty.in_map: This map uses no spline profiles yet.
roadtool.empty.favorites: Mark profiles with the star to find them here.
roadtool.empty.mine: Road types you make with Tools › Road builder... show here.
roadtool.empty.none: No profile of this kind in the installation.
roadtool.crossing.tooltip: On: a click on a road puts a pedestrian crossing into it instead of building a road. A short piece of the same road is cut in with zebra bars and a footpath across it, in one object, so cars give way to people on it. Stored under Sceneryobjects\Mapforge in your OMSI installation.
roadtool.parking.tooltip: On: two clicks on a road put a row of parking spaces along it. The first click picks the start and the side, the second the end. The spaces are car park objects beside the outermost lane, in line with it, so openOMSI's cars can park in and pull out. A map without a parking list gets one.
roadtool.parking.list.tooltip: The parking list the spaces draw their cars from: 0 is the map's own parklist_p.txt, n is parklist_p_n.txt (edit them under Project > Map > Parking list).
roadtool.path_width.tooltip: How wide the paths you draw are, in metres: the corridor people walk in or the strip a vehicle sweeps. A new path type is made from the chosen one and kept in your project.
roadtool.path_both.tooltip: A vehicle path that runs both ways instead of only the way it is drawn.
